{"regions":[{"label":"Figure 1.4 — Data governance layers at the national and international levels","kind":"diagram","bbox":[0.094,0.087,0.797,0.533],"summary":"Four data-governance layers compare policy priorities at national and international levels: infrastructure policies, laws and regulations, economic policies, and institutions.","details":"The diagram has four horizontal rows. Each row pairs an illustrated layer label at left with National and International columns.

• Infrastructure policies — National: “Universal coverage of broadband networks”; “Domestic infrastructure to exchange, store, and process data.” International: “Global technical standards for compatibility of hardware and software”; “Regional collaboration on data infrastructure to achieve scale.”
• Laws and regulations — National: “Safeguards to secure and protect data from the threat of misuse”; “Enablers to facilitate data sharing among different stakeholders.” International: “Cybersecurity conventions for collaboration on tackling cybercrime”; “Interoperability standards to facilitate data exchanges across borders.”
• Economic policies — National: “Antitrust for data platform businesses”; “Trade in data-enabled services”; “Taxation of data platform businesses.” International: “International tax treaties to allocate taxation rights across countries”; “Global trade agreements on cross-border trade in data-enabled services.”
• Institutions — National: “Government entities to oversee, regulate, and secure data”; “Other stakeholders to set standards and increase data access and reuse.” International: “International organizations to support collaboration on data governance and promote standardization”; “Cooperation on cross-border regulatory spillovers and enforcement issues.”
